stem: Which statement about strontium and its compounds is correct?

options.A: Strontium hydroxide is more soluble than barium hydroxide.
options.B: Strontium sulfate is more soluble than magnesium sulfate.
options.C: Strontium nitrate has a lower thermal stability than calcium nitrate.
options.D: Strontium is a stronger reducing agent than magnesium.

stem:
1.0 g of each of four different compounds of Group 2 elements are thermally decomposed. The
residue in each decomposition is the oxide of the Group 2 element.
The volume of gas produced from each reaction is measured at room conditions.
Which substance produces the greatest volume of gas?

options.A: Barium oxide reacts with water at room temperature to form barium hydroxide and hydrogen.
options.B: Calcium oxide does not react with water at room temperature.
options.C: Magnesium hydroxide reacts with steam to form magnesium oxide and hydrogen.
options.D: Strontium oxide reacts with water at room temperature to form strontium hydroxide only.

stem:
W, X, Y and Z are Group 2 elements barium, calcium, magnesium and strontium but not in that
order.
W reacts faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than Y.
The hydroxide of X is less soluble in water than the hydroxide of W.
The sulfate of Y is the most soluble of the sulfates of W, X, Y and Z.
The carbonate of Z decomposes more slowly than the carbonate of W at the same temperature.
What is the Mr of the nitrate of W?

The trends seen in Group 2 can be used to predict the properties of radium and its compounds.
Which statement is correct?

options.A: Radium has the highest second ionisation energy of the elements in Group 2.
options.B: Radium hydroxide is the least soluble of the hydroxides of the elements in Group 2.
options.C: Radium carbonate has the lowest thermal stability of the carbonates of the elements in Group 2.
options.D: Radium reacts faster with water than the other elements in Group 2.
